traits.label: Hymenium
traits.text: Tubular or poroid, with small, angular pores.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium: Tubular or poroid, with small, angular pores.

traits.label: Cap
traits.text: 3-8 cm in diameter. Convex to flat, becoming slightly depressed at maturity; with a zonate pattern, orange-brown to dark brown.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Cap: 3-8 cm in diameter. Convex to flat, becoming slightly depressed at maturity; with a zonate pattern, orange-brown to dark brown.

traits.label: Hymenium attachment
traits.text: Decurrent, extending slightly down the stipe.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium attachment: Decurrent, extending slightly down the stipe.

traits.label: Stipe
traits.text: Cylindrical, central, and somewhat fibrous; the same color or paler than the cap, sometimes with a zonate pattern.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Stipe: Cylindrical, central, and somewhat fibrous; the same color or paler than the cap, sometimes with a zonate pattern.

traits.label: Spore print
traits.text: Spore print: Brown.
traits.raw: 🟤 Spore print: Brown.

traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Saprobic, typically found growing on the ground in coniferous or mixed woods, particularly on well-decayed wood or woody debris.
traits.raw: 🪵 Saprobic, typically found growing on the ground in coniferous or mixed woods, particularly on well-decayed wood or woody debris.

traits.label: Edibility
traits.text: Not considered edible due to its tough texture.
traits.raw: 😖 Not considered edible due to its tough texture.

traits.label: Odour
traits.text: Not distinct.
traits.raw: 👃 Not distinct.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: Up to 8 cm in diameter for the cap, stipe up to 5 cm tall.
traits.raw: 📏 Up to 8 cm in diameter for the cap, stipe up to 5 cm tall.

traits.label: Microscopy
traits.text: Spores are cylindrical to allantoid, 7-9 x 3-4 µm.
traits.raw: 🔬 Spores are cylindrical to allantoid, 7-9 x 3-4 µm.

traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Recognized by its perennial growth habit, zonate pattern on the cap, and its preference for well-decayed wood. The species name "perennis" suggests its perennial nature, meaning it can persist and possibly grow over more than one season.

🌎 Kloostrimetsa, Tallinn, Harju County
🌲🪵 Mixed mostly pine forest, in sandy mossy soil
🍄 Hymenochaetaceae / Agaricomycetes

ℹ️ Hymenium: Tubular or poroid, with small, angular pores.
ℹ️ Cap: 3-8 cm in diameter. Convex to flat, becoming slightly depressed at maturity; with a zonate pattern, orange-brown to dark brown.
ℹ️ Hymenium attachment: Decurrent, extending slightly down the stipe.
ℹ️ Stipe: Cylindrical, central, and somewhat fibrous; the same color or paler than the cap, sometimes with a zonate pattern.
🟤 Spore print: Brown.
🪵 Saprobic, typically found growing on the ground in coniferous or mixed woods, particularly on well-decayed wood or woody debris.
😖 Not considered edible due to its tough texture.
👃 Not distinct.
📏 Up to 8 cm in diameter for the cap, stipe up to 5 cm tall.
🔬 Spores are cylindrical to allantoid, 7-9 x 3-4 µm.
🔤 Recognized by its perennial growth habit, zonate pattern on the cap, and its preference for well-decayed wood. The species name "perennis" suggests its perennial nature, meaning it can persist and possibly grow over more than one season.
